Upstream: the Android Open Source Project's external/svox, pico/lib.
Taken from: Adafruit_CircuitPython_PicoTTS's src/svox/
  https://github.com/adafruit/Adafruit_CircuitPython_PicoTTS
  commit 3496a5d81d3984bacf4876c51653493f5afab867, identical.
That copy came from the ESP-IDF component esp32_picotts
  https://github.com/lllucius/esp32_picotts
  commit 072b3d00f2a5a032bd7f8a517168eb28c41b9b51 (components/picotts/lib)

Files: every .c and .h of pico/lib.

Changes, none of them made here:

1. esp32_picotts added pico_loadMemoryResource() and pico_defineVoice() to
   picoapi.c and picoapi.h, which load a voice from memory instead of a file,
   and ESP-IDF partition and file loaders beside them.
2. Adafruit added a file-less platform, PICO_CIRCUITPY, in picopltf.h, with
   stub file functions in picopal.c; put the ESP-IDF loaders in picoapi.c and
   picoapi.h behind PICO_PLATFORM == PICO_ESP; made IMPLEMENT_TIMER's test
   tolerate an undefined macro in picopal.c; and turned a debug-only static
   counter in picosig.c into a local.

picotts builds with PICO_PLATFORM=PICO_CIRCUITPY on every port: the voice is
read into memory by the Python side and handed to the engine, so nothing in
the engine opens a file.
